title: Lokesh Kanagaraj Is Making a Superhero Film With Aamir Khan. It's Aimed at the World.
excerpt: The LCU architect confirmed the collaboration to The Hollywood Reporter India. Shooting starts next year, and the man who built Vikram's universe says this will 'bring about a new genre.'
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Lokesh Kanagaraj is directing a superhero film starring Aamir Khan, aimed at a global audience.
  • Aamir Khan will shoot three films back-to-back, including a biopic and the superhero project.
  • The film will not be part of Lokesh's Cinematic Universe, allowing creative freedom.
  • Aamir's ambitious slate includes adaptations of iconic Indian stories like the Mahabharata.
  • Lokesh's films have successfully crossed language barriers, appealing to international audiences.
There are collaborations that sound interesting. And then there are collaborations that sound like someone is trying to rearrange the DNA of an entire industry. **Lokesh Kanagaraj** making a superhero film with **Aamir Khan** falls firmly in the second category. The director — who turned Tamil cinema inside out with the interconnected madness of *Kaithi*, *Vikram*, and *Leo*, and who just wrapped **Rajinikanth's** gangster action drama *Coolie* — has now officially confirmed that his Bollywood debut will star the man who once moved an entire nation to wrestle with *Dangal*. The genre? Superhero. The ambition? Global. > "It is a Hindi film, but made for a global audience. Aamir sir and I have spoken about it a lot over the last few months, especially when he was on the sets of Coolie. I found a lot of similarities between him and Kamal Sir. I know fundamentally his films are very different from mine, but our collaboration will bring about a new genre." — Lokesh Kanagaraj, The Hollywood Reporter India Let that sink in. The director who built the most successful cinematic universe in Indian film history is comparing Aamir Khan to **Kamal Haasan** — the man at the centre of *Vikram*. And he's doing it while announcing a film that will attempt something India has never convincingly pulled off: a superhero film with genuine global reach. ## The Timing Is Insane ![Aamir Khan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Aamir_Khan_at_the_success_bash_of_Secret_Superstar.jpg) > **"I know fundamentally his films are very different from mine, but our collaboration will bring about a new genre." — Lokesh Kanagaraj, The Hollywood Reporter India Let that sink in."** Aamir Khan isn't easing back into work after *Sitaare Zameen Par*. He's sprinting. The actor has confirmed he'll shoot three films back-to-back starting this September: First up is the **Dadasaheb Phalke biopic** with **Rajkumar Hirani** — a reunion of the *3 Idiots* and *PK* duo that alone would headline any year. That starts filming in October 2026. Then there's **Lalkaara**, which reunites him with **Ashutosh Gowariker** for a biopic on India's first Test cricket captain, **Lala Amarnath**, with **Farhan Akhtar** co-starring. And somewhere after those two, the Lokesh film goes on floors. Aamir himself has said the superhero project is likely to start in the second half of 2026, around September or October, for a 2027 release. But Lokesh has his own runway to clear first — *Coolie* drops on August 14, and **Karthi's** *Kaithi 2* starts by the end of this year. The realistic timeline puts the Aamir film in 2027 production, possibly 2028 release. And then, looming behind all of it like a final-boss reveal, there's the **Mahabharata**. Aamir has confirmed he's beginning development on a cinematic adaptation of the epic this August, which he'll produce and likely star in. It's the kind of project that sounds like a punchline until you remember this is the man who spent years on *Lagaan*. ## What It Means for the Diaspora For Indian audiences abroad, this announcement carries particular weight. Lokesh Kanagaraj's films have already broken through language barriers — *Vikram* and *Leo* drew packed houses in international markets that historically ignored Tamil cinema. Pair that sensibility with Aamir Khan, who remains arguably the most globally recognised Indian actor (remember, *Dangal* earned over ₹2,000 crore worldwide and became a cultural phenomenon in China), and you have a film engineered to travel. ![The Hollywood Reporter India — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/2/28/19_May_2021_The_Hollywood_Reporter_Cover.jpg)
Aamir Khan's Upcoming Film Slate
September 2026
Starts filming the superhero film with Lokesh Kanagaraj.
October 2026
Begins filming Dadasaheb Phalke biopic with Rajkumar Hirani.
After October 2026
Filming Lalkaara, a biopic on Lala Amarnath.
August 2023
Starts development on Mahabharata adaptation.
The superhero genre is the key variable. India has attempted superhero films before — *Krrish*, *Ra.One*, *Brahmastra*, *Mard Ko Dard Nahi Hota* each took a swing with wildly different results. None achieved what a Marvel or DC film does at the global box office. Lokesh and Aamir appear to know this. The emphasis on "global audience" in every public statement suggests they're not trying to make an Indian superhero film. They're trying to make a superhero film that happens to be Indian. Notably, the Aamir-Lokesh film will **not** be part of the Lokesh Cinematic Universe. While Lokesh has confirmed that *Kaithi 2*, *Vikram 2*, the Rolex spinoff with **Suriya**, and a potential *Leo 2* with **Thalapathy Vijay** all sit within the LCU, the Aamir superhero project is a standalone. That's a deliberate choice — and one that frees the film from franchise obligations. ## The Bigger Picture What Aamir Khan is building right now is the most ambitious slate any Indian star has announced in recent memory. A Hirani biopic. A Gowariker period drama. A Lokesh Kanagaraj superhero film. And the *Mahabharata*. Each one is a potential landmark. Together, they signal an actor who's decided his sixties are going to be the most productive decade of his career.
Lokesh Kanagaraj's Cinematic Universe
›Lokesh's films include Kaithi, Vikram, and Leo.
›Upcoming projects: Kaithi 2, Vikram 2, and Rolex spinoff.
›Aamir's superhero film is a standalone project.
›Lokesh aims to create a new genre with Aamir.
And Lokesh? At 37, with seven films and an entire cinematic universe behind him, he's still finding new worlds to conquer. His Bollywood debut isn't a side quest. It's the next frontier. The film hasn't been titled yet. No cast beyond Aamir has been announced. But the combination of these two minds, in this genre, with this level of ambition? The real superpower might be the collaboration itself.
